name: A-level Economics
tagline: AQA A-level Economics (7136), one short lesson per spec point.
subject: economics

4.1.1.name: Economic methodology and the economic problem
4.1.1.blurb: What economics is, scarcity, opportunity cost and production possibility diagrams.

4.1.2.name: Individual economic decision making
4.1.2.blurb: Rational choice and utility, imperfect information, and what behavioural economics adds.

4.1.3.name: Price determination in a competitive market
4.1.3.blurb: Demand, supply, elasticity, equilibrium and how markets affect each other.

4.1.4.name: Production, costs and revenue
4.1.4.blurb: How firms produce, what it costs them, what they earn and how technology changes it all.

4.1.5a.name: Market structures: perfect competition to monopoly
4.1.5a.blurb: From perfect competition to monopoly: how the number of rivals shapes prices and profits.

4.1.5b.name: Competition, efficiency and welfare
4.1.5b.blurb: Who wins from competition: price discrimination, contestable markets, efficiency and welfare.

4.1.6.name: The labour market
4.1.6.blurb: How wages and jobs are set, and what unions, big employers and the law do to them.

4.1.7.name: The distribution of income and wealth: poverty and inequality
4.1.7.blurb: Who gets what: measuring inequality, understanding poverty and what governments can do.

4.1.8a.name: How markets work and why they fail
4.1.8a.blurb: How prices coordinate an economy, and why markets sometimes get it wrong.

4.1.8b.name: Market imperfections and government action
4.1.8b.blurb: What governments can do about market failure, and how their fixes can go wrong.

4.2.1.name: The measurement of macroeconomic performance
4.2.1.blurb: What governments aim for, and how we measure whether an economy is doing well.

4.2.2.name: How the macroeconomy works: the circular flow of income, aggregate demand/aggregate supply analysis and related concepts
4.2.2.blurb: How the whole economy works: the circular flow, AD and AS, and the multiplier.

4.2.3.name: Economic performance
4.2.3.blurb: Growth, the cycle, jobs and prices, and why they can pull against each other.

4.2.4.name: Financial markets and monetary policy
4.2.4.blurb: Money, banks, the Bank of England and how the financial system is kept safe.

4.2.5.name: Fiscal policy and supply-side policies
4.2.5.blurb: How governments use spending, tax and reform to shape the economy.

4.2.6.name: The international economy
4.2.6.blurb: Trade, exchange rates, globalisation and development: the UK in the world economy.

exam.name: Exam technique
exam.blurb: How the papers work, and how to turn what you know into marks.
